projection.basis: reports/1-profile.md shares (fast tier: 1,800 s run evaluate 3.0, reinit 2.9, pyrogenic 8.4 %; 4 h run 13.6, 10.1, 9.2 % of the katoomba6-fast step loop); every other phase taken as no faster

gate.bar: Gate 1, fast tier: projected whole-step gain >= 1.2x over the best TypeScript arm (its faithful random draw order caps it near 1.3x on 4 cores)
gate.measured: projection 1.099x at the 30-minute shares and 1.217x at the 4 h shares with the best form of each of the three kernels (Amdahl ceilings 1.167x and 1.490x); assumes the rest of the step is no faster
gate.why: a kernel-only projection on the container's shared cores, against one TypeScript thread; the embers (24 % at 30 minutes) stay serial in the faithful draw order; the whole-step measurement is T6.4 / T6.6

notRun: arm64 execution (the android-arm64 build only proves the library compiles; it needs the phone, round 1)
the other fast-tier phases (embers, wind for the fire, moisture, picture, detectors)
WebAssembly timing in Chromium and in the phone WebView (T1.6b; only Node 22 here)
the fire model hook (prepareCell) is not ported: the evaluate benchmark answers the lazy speed requests with the coefficients the real hook wrote (recorded)
CoreMathSharp as the default FsMath: the pyrogenic sine tables would then differ from Node 22 in the last bit and need the test-only shim; with the default (fdlibm) the tables equal Node 22 exactly

conditions.columns: name before|after: UTC time, load average over 1, 5 and 15 minutes (/proc/loadavg); the BenchmarkDotNet sessions run 4 threads in the Parallel cases, which is part of their own load

threadCurve.method: stopwatch, 400 single operations after 400 ms warm-up, median

wasmNode.method: median of the two runs of each side (A B B A: TypeScript, WebAssembly, WebAssembly, TypeScript; every run a fresh process; 1,000 single operations after a 1.5 s warm-up)

k6f-900.wasmRuntime: .NET 11.0.0; rid browser-wasm; dynamicCode False; vector128 True

k6f-late.wasmRuntime: .NET 11.0.0; rid browser-wasm; dynamicCode False; vector128 True

tests.note: dotnet test --project Fs.Tests -c Release; includes the child-process runs (AVX2, AVX-512, hardware intrinsics, tiering, PGO and OSR off), the 9-form bit-equality tests on the real frames and the mutation tests
